questions.question: In the Erlang B model ($M/M/c/c$ queue: Poisson arrivals at rate $\lambda$, $c$ servers with exponential service times of rate $\mu$, no waiting room), what happens to a job that arrives while all $c$ servers are busy?
options: It waits in a queue until the first server becomes free.
It is served by the next server at a reduced service rate.
It is blocked and lost; it never enters the system.
It retries after an exponential time and then joins the system.

questions.question: A hospital ward is modelled as an Erlang B system ($M/M/c/c$ queue) with $c$ identical beds, offered load $a=\lambda/\mu$ and blocking probability $B(c,a)$. Which expression gives the long-run fraction of time that one particular bed is occupied?
options: $a(1-B(c,a))/c$, the mean number of occupied beds divided by $c$
$a/c$, the offered load divided by the number of beds
$1-B(c,a)$, the fraction of time at which not every bed is occupied
$1-p(0)$, the fraction of time at which the ward is not empty

questions.question: In the Erlang B model ($M/M/c/c$ queue: Poisson arrivals at rate $\lambda$, $c$ servers with exponential service times of rate $\mu$, no waiting room), $p(c)$ is the long-run fraction of time that all $c$ servers are busy. Why is $p(c)$ also the long-run fraction of arriving jobs that is blocked?
options: Because each server is busy a fraction $p(c)$ of the time.
Because the blocked jobs are exactly the jobs that see an empty system.
Because the time fraction and the arrival fraction are equal in every queue.
Because Poisson arrivals see time averages (PASTA).

questions.question: In the Erlang B model ($M/M/c/c$ queue: Poisson arrivals at rate $\lambda$, $c$ servers with exponential service times of rate $\mu$, no waiting room), what is the total departure rate $\mu(n)$ when $n$ jobs are present, $0\leq n\leq c$?
options: $\mu(n)=\mu$, because jobs leave one at a time
$\mu(n)=n\mu$, because all $n$ jobs are in service
$\mu(n)=\mu/n$, because the $n$ jobs share the capacity

questions.question: In the Erlang B model ($M/M/c/c$ queue: Poisson arrivals at rate $\lambda$, $c$ servers with exponential service times of rate $\mu$, no waiting room), what is the expected number of jobs waiting in queue, $\mathbb{E}[Q]$?
For the Erlang B model with $c=3$ servers and offered load $a=\lambda/\mu=2$, what is the long-run fraction of time $p(0)$ that all servers are idle, rounded to three decimals?
Calls arrive at a loss system as a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=4$ per hour, and each call lasts on average $\mathbb{E}[S]=30$ minutes. What is the offered load $a=\lambda\mathbb{E}[S]$?
Requests arrive at an Erlang B system at rate $\lambda=2$ per hour, and the blocking probability is $B(c,a)=0.25$. At what long-run rate are requests lost?
In the Erlang B model with offered load $a=\lambda/\mu=4$ and $c=5$ servers, what is the ratio $p(3)/p(2)$ of the stationary probabilities of having $3$ jobs and $2$ jobs present?

A ward modelled as an Erlang B system has offered load $a=3$, with blocking probabilities $B(3,3)=0.346$, $B(5,3)=0.110$, $B(6,3)=0.052$, $B(7,3)=0.022$ and $B(8,3)=0.0081$. What is the smallest number of beds $c$ with $B(c,3)\leq0.05$?
options: $c=3$, as many beds as the offered load

questions.question: In the Erlang B model ($M/M/c/c$ queue: Poisson arrivals at rate $\lambda$, $c$ servers with exponential service times of rate $\mu$, no waiting room), the arrival rate $\lambda$ is doubled while the mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S]$ is halved, with $c$ fixed. What happens to the blocking probability $B(c,a)$?
options: It doubles, because twice as many jobs arrive per unit time.
It halves, because the servers are freed twice as fast.
It increases, because the arrivals are more bursty at higher rate.
It stays the same, because $a=\lambda\mathbb{E}[S]$ is unchanged.

questions.question: Consider the Erlang B model with fixed offered load $a=\lambda/\mu$ and let the number of servers $c\to\infty$. What do the stationary probabilities $p(n)$ tend to?
options: $p(n)\to0$ for every $n$, since the mass spreads out

questions.question: In the Erlang B model ($M/M/c/c$ queue: Poisson arrivals at rate $\lambda$, $c$ servers with exponential service times of rate $\mu$, no waiting room), let $\lambda(n)$ be the rate at which jobs arrive at the system while $n$ jobs are present, and $\lambda^+(n)$ the rate at which arriving jobs actually enter the system in state $n$. Which values are correct in the full state $n=c$?

A single-server loss system ($c=1$, no waiting room) has Poisson arrivals with rate $\lambda$ and exponential service with rate $\mu=1$ per hour. What is the largest $\lambda$ for which the blocking probability is at most $0.2$?

An Erlang B system has offered load $a=2$ and blocking probability $B(3,2)\approx0.2105$ with $3$ servers. The target blocking probability is at most $0.10$. Using the recursion that computes $B(c,a)$ from $B(c-1,a)$, do $4$ servers meet the target?

Two separate Erlang B systems each have $1$ server, $\lambda=1$ and $\mu=1$, so each has $B(1,1)=1/2$. They are merged into one Erlang B system with $2$ servers, arrival rate $2$ and $\mu=1$. What is the blocking probability of the merged system?
Let $N\sim\operatorname{Pois}(a)$ with $a=\lambda/\mu$. Which expression equals the Erlang B blocking probability $B(c,a)$ for $c$ servers?
An Erlang B system has $c=2$ servers, arrival rate $\lambda=10$ and service rate $\mu=1$, so the offered load $a=10$ exceeds $c$. Which statement about its stationary probabilities $p(n)$ is correct?
options: They do not exist, since stability requires $\lambda<c\mu$.
They exist only if blocked jobs are counted in the state.
They exist, since the state space $\{0,1,2\}$ is finite.
They exist only after rescaling time so that $a<1$.

questions.question: Jobs arrive at rate $\lambda=1$ to a loss system without waiting room. System A has $2$ servers with service rate $\mu=1$ each; System B has $1$ server with service rate $\mu=2$. Which system blocks a smaller fraction of the jobs?
options: B, because A loses $0.6$ of jobs and B only $1/3$
A, which loses $0.2$ of jobs against $1/3$ for B
B, since A acts as one rate-$1$ server with $B=0.5$

questions.question: An Erlang B system has $c=2$ servers, $\lambda=3$ per hour and $\mu=1$ per hour. What is the mean number of busy servers $\mathbb{E}[L]$, rounded to two decimals?
